item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00397","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C06","C12"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.88,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 plausibly supplied a material drafting template: both veto memoranda reject special treatment within a Veterans' Administration system because similarly situated people would be governed differently, insist that any remedy should be made through general legislation, and invoke administrative uniformity. C06 uses a closely parallel single-industry-versus-general-relief argument, while C12 supplies a broader veterans-benefits inequity framework, but neither matches the child's compact reasoning as closely as C02.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the principles and rules of administration prescribed in the general law should be set aside except in unique and most compelling circumstances of equity","parent_excerpt":"It would have affected only certain employees of one agency, whereas the same problem confronts many other agencies, and should be dealt with by general legislation.","explanation":"Both reject an exceptional remedy for a limited class when the underlying issue extends to others governed by a general statutory system."},{"child_excerpt":"If the law is to be changed, it should be changed for all.","parent_excerpt":"the same problem confronts many other agencies, and should be dealt with by general legislation.","explanation":"This is the same central drafting proposition: reform should apply generally rather than through a special measure."},{"child_excerpt":"require unswerving uniformity of rule and equality of treatment to all who are similarly situated","parent_excerpt":"This would have been a step toward uncoordinated and diverse pay scales for Government employees, when the need is for greater uniformity.","explanation":"The memoranda share distinctive reliance on uniformity as the reason to veto special treatment."}]}
